status: Engineering/source review; not a fresh model extraction, canonical correction, or universal schema validation
question: Which preparation and molecular distinctions must remain retrievable for a scientist comparing sequencing technologies?

read_scope.page_numbering: one-based PDF page; matches printed page for these pages
read_scope.revisit_reason: User challenges proposed Material State fields; reassess whether comparison-defining distinctions are representable and source wording is reliable. No repeat model extraction.
read_scope.primary_scope: Selected primary-source abstract, figure, results, discussion, or Methods passages retrieved through indexed full-text views. Not full independent review of all eight primary papers or supplements. Some direct PMC opens returned CAPTCHA; indexed primary-source text supplied the stated passages.

methods.material_distinction: Template DNA and random DNA primers are different participants despite both being DNA. Primer resistance to exonuclease must not be represented as extension blocking.
methods.before_after: Primed DNA template becomes displaced amplification products; polymerase is not the material product.
methods.scientific_query: Which priming systems survive a proofreading polymerase while retaining extension competence?
methods.source_issue: Illumina labels the primers 3-prime blocked. Its cited Dean2001 primary instead describes thiophosphate protection against exonuclease and successful extension. Preserve source wording, but do not canonically encode an extension-blocked primer.
methods.primary_scope: Results, Figure 1, Discussion and selected Methods passages; original study is multiply-primed RCA and should not establish every modern MDA variant.

methods.material_distinction: Genomic template, semi-amplicon and full amplicon have different sequence architecture and amplification behavior. Full amplicon terminal sequences hybridize intramolecularly.
methods.before_after: Primer extension creates semi-amplicons, then full amplicons; terminal complementarity permits looping before the later PCR stage.
methods.scientific_query: Which amplification designs reduce re-amplification of completed products, and what product structure causes it?
methods.do_not_conflate: A hybridized loop is not automatically a covalently closed DNA circle. A single strandedness label cannot describe all regions of the structure.
methods.primary_scope: Figure 1 and surrounding amplification comparison passages.

methods.material_distinction: DNA entering bisulfite treatment lacks sequencing adaptors; adaptors are introduced afterward through random-primer extension.
methods.before_after: Bisulfite-treated DNA is used for post-conversion adaptor tagging rather than exposing already tagged templates to the damaging treatment.
methods.scientific_query: Which methods change adaptor-addition order to reduce loss of sequenceable templates?
methods.do_not_conflate: Same DNA class and same listed operations do not imply equivalent workflow; adaptor presence at the conversion boundary and operation order matter.
methods.primary_scope: Primary abstract and figure material; direct full-text open was blocked. No full-paper verification claimed.

methods.material_distinction: The tagmented preparation must have methylated adaptor sequence and the relevant covalent attachment on each strand before bisulfite exposure.
methods.before_after: Tagmented DNA undergoes oligonucleotide replacement and repair to obtain bisulfite-compatible tagged templates.
methods.scientific_query: Which changes make a tagmentation product usable in a bisulfite workflow?
methods.do_not_conflate: Adapter-tagged DNA is insufficient: a hybridized oligonucleotide and a covalently attached strand have different survival through denaturation and conversion.
methods.primary_scope: Original 2012 Tn5mC-seq abstract/design passage; Illumina cites the later Wang2013 T-WGBS protocol. Shared design claim only, not identity of every recipe/version.

methods.material_distinction: 5hmC-containing DNA is chemically changed before bisulfite; comparison with a matched ordinary bisulfite branch supports the 5hmC estimate.
methods.before_after: Oxidation changes 5hmC to 5fC; downstream base readout differs from the untreated-with-oxidant branch.
methods.scientific_query: Which observed bases distinguish original modifications, and which comparison branch is required?
methods.do_not_conflate: Modified-base populations within one preparation are not separate isolated fractions. Two processing branches are separate even if both are simply named DNA.
methods.support_status: Illumina description read; original Booth2012 not independently read here. Primary redBS study by Booth et al. corroborates prior oxBS mechanism and comparison requirement.

methods.material_distinction: The identity and origin of each base modification must remain linked: protected 5hmC versus 5mC oxidized to 5caC before bisulfite.
methods.before_after: Glucosylation protects one base class while oxidation makes another class convertible; both classes remain in the same DNA preparation.
methods.scientific_query: What chemically distinguishes protection of the target from conversion of competing modifications?
methods.do_not_conflate: DNA plus modified base is not enough, and unchanged sequence identity is not unchanged chemical identity. Reporter base must remain linked to its precursor modification.
methods.primary_scope: Indexed article metadata and targeted glucosylation/oxidation passages only; no complete primary paper verification.

methods.material_distinction: Protein-crosslinked, immunoselected chromatin and purified DNA are not interchangeable inputs to exonuclease footprinting. The protein barrier establishes where trimming stops.
methods.before_after: On-resin ChIP material with an initial adaptor is exonuclease-trimmed; crosslink reversal and subsequent library operations follow in the primary protocol.
methods.scientific_query: Which change shifts positional information from random fragment boundaries to a protein-associated exonuclease boundary?
methods.source_issue: Grouped Illumina page places exonuclease before immunoprecipitation and assigns it to a broad ChIP schematic. Primary ChIP-exo protocol describes exonuclease after ChIP on resin. Do not distribute grouped operations across all named members or publish source order as canonical without qualification.
methods.primary_scope: Indexed primary protocol Figure 1 caption; corroborating Methods in https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5880240/ . Original 2011 paper direct open blocked.

methods.material_distinction: Native chromatin context is needed when accessibility is recorded; after treatment, introduced GpC methylation and endogenous CpG methylation can be read from extracted DNA.
methods.before_after: A chromatin-accessibility distinction becomes a chemical mark on the DNA; extraction later removes chromatin context without necessarily removing that recorded mark.
methods.scientific_query: Which methods preserve an earlier protein-accessibility distinction in a DNA readout, and can it be associated with endogenous methylation on the same molecule?
methods.do_not_conflate: Methylation as an assay-introduced reporter differs from methylation as the native analyte, even though their chemistry is the same. Overlapping sequence contexts require disambiguation in analysis.
methods.primary_scope: Primary abstract, library-construction Methods and within-read GCH/HCG analysis passages.

cross_case_findings: A substance list cannot establish a useful scientific state. DNA may be template, primer, adapter, amplified copy, endogenous analyte or reporter; the role belongs to a specified operation or measurement.
The scientifically useful record starts with the actual preparation being handed between operations. Structural facts are attached to named material parts rather than to an undifferentiated mixture.
An introduced mark requires both chemical identity and production provenance. NOMe-seq shows why modification chemistry alone cannot distinguish biological analyte from experimental reporter.

Sequence constructs need a representation of relevant segments and their connection, orientation or pairing. MALBAC and T-WGBS cannot be compared reliably using only DNA, single-stranded and adapter-present labels.
A State requires source-qualified facts at a workflow boundary. False certainty from broad normalization is a bigger risk than temporarily retaining a source-qualified description.
Graph evolution requires an explicit before/after comparison of those facts and operation order, not an edge inferred from common material types.

minimal_contract_recommendation.status: Proposal for parent review, not implemented
minimal_contract_recommendation.scientist_facing_start: Name the actual preparation/product and the operation that produced or consumes it; e.g. bisulfite-treated untagged DNA, crosslinked immunoselected chromatin on resin, or tagmented DNA with methylated covalent adaptors.
mandatory_common_information: Which preparation is being passed, with source evidence and exact workflow boundary
Which material part is acted on and its local role
Which supported structural, chemical, contextual or association facts are required to understand the next operation or the claimed difference
What measurement association or encoded information survives, with experimental origin and carrier
Which fractions are genuinely separate; do not split coexisting chemical classes

conditional_property_groups.nucleic_acid_construct: Polymer, strand/segment organization, end chemistry, sequence handles, modifications and relevant covalent versus hybridized connections
conditional_property_groups.chromatin_preparation: Native or crosslinked preparation, selected protein-associated population, accessibility context, support and crosslink-removal boundary
conditional_property_groups.chemical_encoding: Precursor modification, introduced derivative, selective protection/conversion, comparator branch, observed base and inference

minimal_contract_recommendation.why_conditional: Do not require exhaustive features for every state. Require the properties that the operation class and specific comparison depend upon, recording unknown rather than inventing a value. Retain source grouping unless it prevents answering the concrete comparison.
meaningful_negative_controls: Reject equating extendable exonuclease-protected primers with extension-blocked primers
Reject identifying hybridization-looped MALBAC amplicons as covalently circular DNA
Reject treating tagmented DNA with merely hybridized oligos as bisulfite-ready covalently tagged strands
Reject treating native and experimentally introduced cytosine methylation as the same measurement
Reject assigning exonuclease digestion to every member of an Illumina grouped ChIP card
Reject collapsing oxBS and BS processing branches because both contain genomic DNA
